messages:
alex wong: quick q about flag precedence — we have flags at org / project / model / route levels. what's the canonical override order?

maria gonzalez: most-specific wins is the rule we've been using (route > model > project > org) :+1:

cheng li: +1 but two caveats: 1) some boolean flags use 'opt-in' semantics at higher levels so absence != false, 2) canary audiences can short-circuit if routed by user id or segment (so evaluation can be context-dependent)

alex wong: got it. example: `feature_x.enabled` set true at org, false at project, route none, model none — result = false, right?

maria gonzalez: correct. project-level false overrides org true. route/model only override if present.

priya rao: one more nuance — how do we treat lists/objects? e.g., `feature_x.allowed_models = ["gpt-4o", "gpt-3-ql"]` at org and project adds "redwood-compat". do we merge or replace?

samir patel: currently we replace for non-scalar types (we treat arrays/objects as atomic). merging would be nicer but risky. we should decide case-by-case.

alex wong: hmmm that could break some customers if we change semantics. would prefer explicit merge flags like `merge_strategy: append` if we ever implement it.

cheng li: also watch caching: evaluation cache uses key = (tenant, project, route, model, flag_key). if we change semantics we need cache invalidation rules.

alex wong: here's a snippet of proposed spec I'm planning to add to the flag-service README — want sanity check:
```
# precedence order (high -> low)
1. route: path+method specific overrides
2. model: model id / family overrides
3. project: project-scoped overrides
4. org: org-wide defaults

# semantics
- scalar flags: last-write wins (most-specific wins)
- object/array flags: replace by default, optional `merge_strategy` allowed
- absent flag at a level => falls back to next lower specificity
- canary audiences evaluated before final boolean if rule present
```

maria gonzalez: looks good. add a note about safety: route-level overrides should not be used for long-lived feature flips, only short-term canaries. put rollback docs link. :eyes:

samir patel: also add a migration script to detect existing overlaps (org vs project vs model vs route) and warn when an override exists. i can take that.

priya rao: for guardrails: suggests automatic cascade-off for sensitive flags — e.g., `pi_access` cannot be enabled at route without org-level approval. we should enforce via validation hooks.

cheng li: agree. we can add a `policy` field on flag metadata: `[allow_override: boolean, require_approval: boolean, max_canary_percent: int]` — validated at write time.

alex wong: @maria can we get this spec added to the docs + a small migration task? would like to start a 5% canary on /v1/generate for model `redwood-rlhf-v2` once we have validations.

maria gonzalez: sure, i'll file a doc PR and a backlog ticket for validation + migration.

deploy-bot: deploy started — feature-flag-service/validate-metadata v1.6.3 -> prod (by cheng)

alex wong: awesome — canary plan: 5% -> 10% after 2h if error rate < 0.5% and latency within SLA. pinging @samir @priya for ops runbook review.

samir patel: LGTM, i will review the ops runbook now. :thumbsup:

priya rao: reviewing, will add emergency cutoff steps and a snippet to force-off a route-level override (`POST /flags/{key}/force-off?scope=route&route=/v1/generate`).

maria gonzalez: added doc PR link in #docs when ready. I'll also add the example JSON for `policy` fields.

alex wong: thanks all. i'll hold on canary until validations are merged. will post follow-up here when ready. :pray:
